title: Midwatch Sentinel: Annotated Shift Summary
content:
Purpose:
Quick midwatch summary for the on-call rotation (02:00–06:00 UTC) — notes intended for the incoming morning watch. Focus: a transient latency surge affecting EU-hosted inference routes, actions taken, immediate mitigations, and runbook gaps discovered.

High-level summary:
- Pager: PAGER-4635 triggered at 02:13 UTC for increased p50/p95 on /v1/generate (eu-west-1).
- Impact: 4–8% of requests experienced >500ms extra tail latency for ~24 minutes; elevated error budget consumption on hosted tier A customers. No widespread 5xx spike observed.
- Root-cause hypothesis (initial): coordinated KV cache TTL expiry + autoscaler pool churn during a scheduled capacity rebalance job.
- Current state: traffic back to normal, synthetic checks green, but follow-ups required to avoid recurrence.

Timeline (concise):
- 02:13 UTC — Pager fires: alert rule multiregion-latency-eu p95 > 350ms for 3m. Oncall Marcus acknowledged.
- 02:16 UTC — Confirmed pattern in traces: increased decoder token processing time and repeat model load events. Spike correlated with a cache-miss flood for prefix/KV store for a small subset of model shards.
- 02:24 UTC — Escalated to infra (Diego) after seeing concurrent pod restarts on a subset of worker pools. Slack thread: #ops-bridge-thread (link above).
- 02:30 UTC — Canary shard restart discovered (k8s rollout of infra/kv-cache v1.7.4) coincident with autoscaler rebalance job kicked by scheduler-alpha.
- 02:36 UTC — Temporary mitigation: scaled up warm pools for affected instance group + pin fallback model variant for heavy routes. Implemented via console run (console-change-1721).
- 02:42 UTC — p95 reduced to normal band; synthetic end-to-end checks pass at 02:48 UTC. Alert auto-resolved at 02:49 UTC.

Immediate actions taken (operational):
- Increased warm pool size for eu-west-1 model workers by +20% to reduce cold starts during rollouts (temporary, to be reverted when follow-up changes are applied). Owner: Diego.
- Rolled back the kv-cache sidecar image on the small subset of nodes to v1.7.3 where observed restarts were absent. Owner: Marcus.
- Deployed a temporary routing rule to divert new sessions for the most latency-sensitive customers to a pin-model fallback (model-x-small) until the warm pool stabilizes. Owner: CustomerReliability (ticketed).

Metrics and evidence collected:
- Traces: sample traces show repeated model artifact download attempts for same session id where previously we had stable KV hits.
- Logs: kubelet logs showed OOMKilled events on 3 nodes at 02:15–02:18 UTC (resource pressure due to cache warmup).
- Dashboards: p50/p95 token latency graphs annotated at event window; savings after warm-pool bump documented.
- Synthetic checks: e2e-generation-eu-01 returned to SLA thresholds by 02:48 UTC.

Runbook gaps discovered (actionable items):
1) Runbook "model-worker-rollout" lacks a preflight step to verify KV cache hit-rate stability during rolling updates. Add a pre-check that monitors KV hit-rate delta and blocks rollout if drop > 10% in last 5m. Suggested owner: eng-serving-runtime.
2) No explicit play for autoscaler-induced mass eviction during rebalance. Create a short play: when a rebalance job is scheduled, rate-limit concurrent pod restarts and prewarm caches incrementally. Owner: infra/autoscaler.
3) Alert tuning: current alert lumps multiple failure modes under a single p95 rule. Add a second alert that triggers on model-load spike (trace-derived) to quickly call infra rather than broad SRE. Owner: eng-sre-alerting.

Follow-ups and tickets (prioritized):
- SRE-4897 (High): Add KV-hit preflight check to model-worker-rollout runbook; include canary-validation queries. Assigned: Aisha. ETA: 2027-12-10.
- SRE-4898 (Medium): Autoscaler rebalance safety: implement staggered node drains + prewarm hook. Assigned: Diego. ETA: 2027-12-17.
- INFRA-337 (Low): Investigate OOM patterns during cache warmup; adjust resource requests for sidecar. Assigned: Priya. ETA: 2027-12-24.
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2213 — rollback patch applied (kv-cache v1.7.3) and a follow-up PR queued to add liveness probe backoff.

Communication notes (for customers & CS):
- Customer-facing impact was limited; CS should proactively reach out to any customers flagged by the pager (list attached in SRE-4897). No credit required per policy but monitor for complaints.
- Draft slack blurbs and postmortem seed will be prepared after follow-ups are triaged.

Runbook draft snippets (to be merged into runbooks/model-worker-rollout.md):
- "Preflight: Before rolling a kv-cache update in any region, run 'kv-hit-check --region=eu-west-1 --window=300s' and ensure hit_rate_drop < 0.10. If threshold exceeded, abort rollout and open INFRA-xxx."
- "Autoscaler rebalance play: When a scheduled rebalance runs, add --stagger=60s and limit concurrent evictions to N/10 where N is number of nodes to be drained. Trigger prewarm workers with --warm=true for 2x expected traffic for 5m post-eviction."

Notes to incoming shift (what to watch next):
- Keep an eye on p95 for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 for next 24h (possible aftershocks during subsequent autoscaler windows).
- Check kubelet OOM pattern: GH Ops dashboard > node-health > eu-west-1 > last 12h.
- Confirm SRE-4897 preflight tests merged before next infra rollout.

Unresolved questions (for postmortem):
- Why did the rollout scheduler pick a small subset of nodes rather than a more even distribution? (scheduler-alpha heuristics?)
- Did the sidecar upgrade include any hidden memory regression? (need bench and image diff).
- Are synthetic checks adequate to detect cache-eviction-induced token latency early enough?

Attachments & useful links:
- Linked artifacts above (Jira, PR, Slack thread).
- Temporary console change: console-change-1721 (internal change log).
- Traces: trace-id: trace-eu-20271130-0216 (internal trace viewer).

Action owners and next steps (short):
- Aisha: drive SRE-4897 (runbook preflight) — blocked until we decide acceptance criteria.
- Diego: INFRA-337 investigation + autoscaler rebalance mitigation prototype.
- Priya: resource request audit for kv-cache sidecar; propose 2 options (raise memory by 20% or add liveness probe backoff).
- Marcus (oncall): prepare initial postmortem skeleton, set follow-up meeting for 2027-12-02 16:00 UTC.

Closing note (tone: practical):
Event was contained with low customer impact due to fast detection and a conservative mitigation strategy (warm-pool bump + rollback). The priority now is tightening rollout safety and adding a simple preflight to prevent cache mass-eviction scenarios. This doc should serve as the source of truth for the morning handoff; merge runbook snippets into the canonical runbook and link the merged PR in SRE-4897 when ready.

---
Meeting/hand-off checklist (tick when done):
- [ ] Confirm warm-pool revert schedule (temporary scale down once follow-ups deployed).
- [ ] Attach postmortem seeds to SRE-4897.
- [ ] Notify CS with templated blurb if customer tickets are raised.

End of midwatch sentinel summary.
